subject: Life Skills
title: Cooper's Color Code
description: A fast breakdown of Cooper's Color Code for builders.

hook.text: Marine Colonel Jeff Cooper created a four-color scale for alertness. Most people live stuck on the wrong color.

buildup.text: White means oblivious — headphones in, eyes on phone. Yellow means relaxed but aware. Most of your day should be yellow.

discovery.text: Orange means a specific threat has your attention. Red means you are acting on it. You need yellow to reach orange.

twist.text: Staying in orange all day is not alertness — it is anxiety. The goal is calm yellow, not constant paranoia.

climax.text: Practice yellow: when you enter a room, note exits and scan faces once. Then relax. That is enough.

punchline.text: Aware, not anxious. Yellow is the sweet spot.

quiz.question: In Cooper's Color Code, what does 'Condition Yellow' mean?
options: Relaxed but alert to your surroundings
